title: Muted sound is unexpectedly unmuted after connecting laptop to a dock
line: Sound and microphones muted with the mute keys now stay muted when a dock, monitor, headset or other audio device is connected.
explanation: With global mute on, kded treated any volume change or unmute on any device as the user ending global mute and unmuted everything. When a device appears, WirePlumber creates it and then restores its saved volume and mute state, so plugging a dock, headset or any new output unmuted all speakers; if the device was the user's chosen output it even becomes the default before that restore. New microphones were also not muted, because handleNewSource() read them from the sink model. Now only changes on the default device that was already there end global mute; devices that global mute had to mute when they appeared (or on a port change), and all non-default devices, are muted again if they get unmuted, until global mute is turned off. The volume keys still end it on any default device, and microphones follow the same rule.

commits.message:
kded: Only let the default device break global mute

Any change on any device broke global mute, even the sound server
restoring a newly plugged device's volume. Only the default device that
was there before breaks it now; other devices, mics too, stay muted.

BUG: 511576

media.caption: Global mute on, then SinkB (not the default) unplugged and plugged back: every output is unmuted
Same steps with the fix: all outputs stay muted
Global mute on, then the chosen output SinkC unplugged and plugged back (it becomes the default again before its volume is restored): every output is unmuted
Same steps with the fix: all outputs stay muted
Microphone mute on, then MicM2 unplugged and plugged back: both microphones are live
Same steps with the fix: both microphones stay muted

review.text: The root cause diagnosis and the handleNewSource() m_sourceModel index fix are spot-on, and the test scenarios confirm that replugged sinks and mics stay muted. However, keeping newly connected or port-switched devices in m_newSinks/m_newSources indefinitely while global mute is active introduces a severe UX regression: clicking Unmute or dragging the volume slider on the default device in the Audio Volume applet or Sound KCM (or scrolling the tray icon) immediately re-mutes itself, leaving users without hardware media keys unable to unmute via normal device controls. Additionally, only adding devices that arrive unmuted misses the case where a previously muted preferred device arrives muted before WirePlumber restores its volume.
changes: Do not permanently block UI unmute/volume changes on newly connected or port-switched default devices (and non-default devices): either end suppression once WirePlumber's initial restore settles, or have explicit user unmute/volume actions from the applet/KCM disable global mute so clicking Unmute or scrolling the tray icon works after plugging in a dock or headphones.

Insert newly added or port-switched devices into the restore-suppression tracking whenever global mute is active, not only when !Muted, so a previously muted preferred device that arrives muted before WirePlumber restores its volume cannot break global mute.

Remove entries from m_newSinks/m_newSources on rowsRemoved (to prevent unbounded growth from transient devices like RAOP/AirPlay sinks) and stop or refresh local globalMute inside the handleSinkDataChanged/handleSourceDataChanged loop after calling disableGlobalSinkMute()/disableGlobalSourceMute().

reviews.text: Right repo and root cause (kded treating WirePlumber's restore on a new device as user intent), it fixes the handleNewSource sink/source model mixup, and the before/after shots for replugged non-default sinks, a replugged chosen default and mics are convincing. But the 'new device' mark never expires until global mute is toggled, so in the bug's own scenario (dock or headset plugged while muted, its output becomes the default) clicking that device's mute button or dragging its slider in the applet or KCM is silently reverted for as long as global mute stays on; the mute key or middle-click are the only ways out. Reverting every unmute of a non-default device is also a visible behaviour change that the commit message understates.
changes: Let the user end global mute from a newly plugged default device once the sound server has finished restoring it, e.g. drop the device from m_newSinks/m_newSources after its restore (the first unmute that kded reverts) instead of keeping it until global mute is toggled, and verify that unmuting the replugged default from the applet then ends global mute.

Mark every device that appears or changes port while global mute is on, not only ones that appear unmuted, so a stored-muted chosen output that becomes the default cannot end global mute through its volume restore.
Have the commit message say that unmuting a non-default device while global mute is on is now reverted, and that new microphones are now muted (handleNewSource used the sink model).
